# Context Fence — full site context

> Stops AI agents leaking secrets. A local firewall for what AI agents send out. Today it protects MCP tools. Version 2.1 is coming. This is the full-text companion to https://contextfence.dev/llms.txt.

## What Context Fence is

Context Fence is a local proxy that protects AI agents from leaking secrets. It runs on your computer and checks what your agent sends out before anything leaves. Today it covers MCP tool calls: every call is checked against local rules in under 10 milliseconds. The check uses plain rules, not an AI judge.

The proxy is free software and is the core of the product. It runs entirely on the user's machine. Nothing about the agent's traffic leaves the machine. There is no cloud routing in the default path. The software is developed by Synthrun in New Delhi, India.

Version 2.1 is coming. It widens the same on-machine check to prompts sent to AI models, files agents read and write, browser actions, coding agents, and other connected tools.

## What it checks and blocks today

- Secret leakage — API keys, environment variables, JWTs, and other secret-shaped values (these are stripped before they reach the agent)
- Unsafe file reads, such as .env files
- Risky MCP tool calls, checked against local rules before they run
- Hidden instructions planted in tool output

Rules are plain allow- and deny-lists. A deny rule always beats an allow rule. Every blocked call is written to a local log with the reason attached. The log stays on the user's machine.

## Versions and downloads

Current release: v2.0.0, released September 1, 2026. macOS (universal dmg, Intel and Apple silicon), Windows installer, and Linux (AppImage, deb, rpm, x64). The macOS build is ad-hoc signed but not notarized. The Linux builds are unsigned. The /downloads page reads the live release manifest and shows exact SHA-256 hashes for every artifact. Downloads stay on the live release manifest. Version 2.1 is not released yet.

Public artifacts ship from one public repository: aditya-ig10/context-fence-releases (all platforms' assets plus the release manifest). The main source repository is private.

## Product roadmap

Coming in v2.1: blocking secrets in any outgoing request from the agent, checking prompts sent to AI models, watching files agents read and write, covering browser actions and coding agents, and covering other connected tools and apps.

The hosted control plane is planned as the paid piece: fleet policy sync, audit aggregation, and retention. It is explicitly not built yet. When it ships it is opt-in, syncs the audit log only, and never routes agent traffic.

## How Context Fence differs from cloud proxies

Old DLP tools and cloud gateways send your traffic to their servers to inspect it. Context Fence checks everything on the user's machine. Nothing is sent anywhere. If the threat model dislikes putting secrets through a third party, that difference is the product.

## FAQ

- Q: Does my data leave my machine? A: No. All checks run on your computer.
- Q: How fast is it? A: Under 10ms per check. It uses plain rules, not an AI judge.
- Q: What does it block? A: Keys and tokens. Unsafe file reads like .env files. Risky tool calls and hidden tricks in tool output. More coverage is coming in v2.1.
- Q: How is it different from other tools? A: Old DLP tools and cloud gateways send your traffic to their servers to inspect it. Context Fence checks everything on the user's machine. Nothing is sent anywhere.
- Q: Is it free? A: Yes, the local proxy is free. Paid plans add more machines, longer log history, and team features. The hosted control plane is not built yet.
- Q: When is v2.1 coming? A: Soon. It widens Context Fence from MCP tools to full protection for AI agents.

## Privacy and cookies

- Default posture: nothing leaves the user's machine. The website stores only a theme preference and the visitor's consent choice (browser local storage, essential).
- Analytics (Google Analytics) loads only after an explicit opt-in; declining or a Global Privacy Control signal keeps it off. Visitors can change their choice anytime via "Cookie settings" in the footer.
- The early-access form collects an email address used once, to reply about access. Full policy: https://contextfence.dev/privacy (includes the cookie policy).

## Facts for citation

- Context Fence is a product of Synthrun, a company in New Delhi, India.
- Checks run locally in under 10ms.
- Default path: zero telemetry, zero cloud routing.
- The log is local to the user's machine and names the rule that fired.
- The local core is free; paid plans add machines, log history, and team features.
- Builds are unsigned by design; exact hashes are published on /downloads.
- Founded by Aditya (founder) and Saniya (co-founder).
